subject: Sentinel: network isolation scenarios & operational validation
messages:
From: Marina Lopez <marina.lopez@sentinel-corp.com>

Cc: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@sentinel-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: isolation scenarios + operator access validation

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team appreciated the clarity on burst capacity and model fallbacks. As we move into procurement, the security reviewers have a few scenario-driven questions for your Private deployment options (VPC and air-gapped). Can you provide written responses and any supporting evidence for the items below?

1) Egress and enforced outbound controls: examples of how you prevent unintended egress from an on-prem/private instance (network-level and OS-level controls).
2) Operator access model: do you support ephemeral operator sessions, MFA + bastion, and separation of duties?
3) Patch and supply-chain assurance: process for applying updates in air-gapped installs, SBOM / provenance.
4) Recovery/rollback: validated playbook for operator errors (credential leakage, accidental firewall rule change).

If possible, include a diagram for the VPC/hybrid network posture and a short operator runbook excerpt. We plan to share this with our InfoSec and Procurement tomorrow afternoon.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — would a two-business-day reply work?

Thanks,
Marina Lopez
Director, Technical Procurement
Sentinel Corp

Attachment: procurement_sentinel_questions.pdf (PDF)

From: nikhil_sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Marina Lopez <marina.lopez@sentinel-corp.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@sentinel-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: isolation scenarios + operator access validation

Marina —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise responses plus pointers to the evidence files attached. I copied Laura for the operational runbook excerpt.

1) Egress and outbound controls
- Network: our Private deployment supports enforced egress restrictions via customer-controlled route tables and NAT configurations; by default we install a deny-by-default iptables filter at the host and require explicit allow rules for approved outbound endpoints. Customers provide an allowlist when air-gapped; we support static-blocking and periodic checksum validation of allowed images via an on-prem proxy.
- OS-level: our operator image runs under an unprivileged container runtime; the management plane processes are confined with SELinux/AppArmor profiles. We ship a hardened baseline and provide automation that validates kernel/module whitelists on start.
- Evidence: see sentinel_evidence_matrix.xlsx (tab 'Network Controls') and vpc-isolation-diagram.png.

2) Operator access model
- Ephemeral sessions: we support short-lived operator certificates via customer KMS; sessions are brokered through a bastion in the customer VPC and require a signed session token.
- MFA & bastion: MFA enforcement is enforced at the identity provider layer (SAML/OIDC) and required for operator elevation. Bastion access integrates with centrally managed IdP and logs are shipped to customer SIEM.
- Separation of duties: operator roles are scoped (deploy, infra, security) and scoped ACLs prevent role overlap. We publish an RBAC matrix in the runbook excerpt.
- Evidence: operator_runbook_draft.md (excerpt), deployment-playbook-v1.pdf.

3) Patch and supply-chain assurance
- Air-gapped updates: we provide a verified update bundle (signed, checksummed) that customers transfer via removable media or secure portal. The bundle includes an SBOM (CycloneDX) and binary hashes; our installer verifies signatures with the customer's configured root CA before applying.
- Provenance: every build artifact is signed by our build system (distinct signing key per release) and we publish build metadata to a read-only registry.
- Evidence: sentinel_evidence_matrix.xlsx (tab 'SBOM & Updates').

4) Recovery & rollback
- Playbooks: validated rollback is supported via image immutability and retained KV snapshots. The playbook describes immediate network lockdown commands and role-specific remediation steps (operator session invalidation, KMS key rotation guidance).
- Dry-run: we recommend and support staged dry-run procedures in a non-prod isolated VLAN; our test harness reproduces firewall-change failure modes.
- Evidence: deployment-playbook-v1.pdf (sections 3–5).

Next steps: I attached a VPC diagram and the evidence matrix. Laura, can you review the runbook excerpt and confirm the operator session TTL defaults? We can join a 30-minute review with the Sentinel InfoSec team tomorrow morning if that helps.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sentinel_evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), vpc-isolation-diagram.png (image), deployment-playbook-v1.pdf (PDF)

Team — forwarding Sentinel's follow-up and Nikhil's draft responses. A few internal notes before we send final:

- Laura: confirm operator TTL (default we used in text is 1 hour for elevated ops; reduce to 15m for air-gapped by policy). Please inline small wording change to the runbook excerpt.
- Priyom: procurement may push for a rolling 90-day notary of SBOMs; can we confirm support for an on-prem signature rotation task? If not currently productized, note a manual operator step.
- Nikhil: include a short excerpt on audit log retention and where telemetry is stored (we need clear language for 'we forward logs to the customer's SIEM only' — highlight that by default we do not lift telemetry to Redwood hosted services for Private installs).

I've attached the runbook draft with inlined comments. Once Laura/Priyom ack I'll merge and send to Marina with a link to the shared Drive folder.

-Vanessa
Senior PM, Deployability
